label: 1-2 steps after an h input, early in the original phase
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the one or two steps right after the letter h was input. It is strongest on the step immediately after h (prev_tok=h gives 13x lift and 65% of activation mass) and weaker two steps after (prev2_tok=h). It is limited to early positions: inputs at t=2..5 carry about 97% of the mass, rates peak at t=4, and it is almost silent after an h that appears late (t>=6). It never fires at t=0/1 or in the copy phase, and only weakly at the delimiter. Magnitude grows when several h tokens appear close together: steps after h h or h h h hold most of the near-max examples and fall heavily in the top quartile, while a single h gives roughly 0.3-0.6 of max. The token currently being input barely matters. On dev, precision is 0.87 and mass recall 0.86. The remaining roughly 40% of active steps are weak activations spread over contexts with no h, plus some steps 3 after an h.

issues: I reproduced the test scores: precision 0.872, recall 0.576, F1 0.694, mass recall 0.865. On the test split, coverage by activation quartile is 0.12 / 0.35 / 0.85 / 0.98, so the predicate captures the strong activations.

Small overstatement about late positions. When h is at t=5, the next step (t=6) is active in 50.7% of cases (dev). The explanation calls this 'almost silent after an h at t>=6', but the predicate's t<=5 cutoff simply drops this case. Real silence only starts for h at t>=6 (t=7 rate 0.001). The t=6 step holds about 3% of the mass, so this is minor.

The rule depends on where the h sits, not just how far back it is. One step after h, precision is about 0.95-1.0 when h is at positions 1-4. Two steps after h, precision is 0.83-0.91 for h at positions 1-3, but only 0.53 for h at position 0 (fires at t=2) and 0.40 for h at position 4. Most of the predicate's false positives are 'h at t=0, predicted at t=2' (h v *c* ..., h a *3* ...).
Three steps after h is a real secondary pattern: precision 0.46 for h at positions 1-2. Adding it for t=4..5 raises test mass recall to 0.907 and F1 to 0.713, but precision drops to 0.78.

The activations with no h are diffuse and weak. In the original phase, steps with no h seen so far fire at a 1.6% rate. They account for 27% of active steps but only 5.7% of activation mass, and they show no lift for any particular token or position. This explains the low recall by count, and it counts as scattered noise, not a systematic missed class.

These claims checked out: no copy-phase activations (0 of 2.7M steps); no activations at t=0 or t=1; the delimiter carries only 1.9% of mass, all of it at steps right after an h (0.15 precision there); the input token is irrelevant (in_tok lifts are all about 1.1-1.4x); the rate peaks at t=4; and the top examples all come from h h / h h h contexts.
skeptic.revised_label: 1-2 steps after an h input in the original phase, for h at positions 1-5 (h at position 0 only fires 2 steps later)
